newsitem.title: UK: Bradford wool market sees firmer trend.
newsitem.headline: Bradford wool market sees firmer trend.

text.p: At what are nominally the first sales of a new season in Australia, but seen in the trade as the closing sales of the 1996/97 season, wool prices regained firmness and for some categories tended dearer.
This was welcomed ahead of the three week recess before sales start again in earnest, since it creates a more confident background for new business if anyone has anything to cover.
A weaker close would be more likely to lead to new orders being postponed in case lower prices applied in August. At present little or no business is being reopened in the trade.
Holidays are increasingly having their usual effect, in regions around the UK and for longer spells in countries on the Continent.

The UK industry is keeping busy meeting a good call for deliveries of old ordcrs and some sectors are under pressure to keep up with this, but little new is following on. The central problem for the UK industry is strength in sterling. This means that exports are increasingly overpriced compared with competition, and that even in the home market competitive imports are a growing threat.

The Budget this week did not help this aspect, since sterling strengthened further, with further interest rate rises seen. It had been hoped that fiscal measures might have been enough to reduce the need for interest rate rises and thus check strength in sterling.

Prices for semi-processed products quoted in the IJIC are poised between cheapening due to the sterling effect and firmness due to the wool price tendency. Many are unchanged and adjustrnents are small.
